subject: Hosted commit uplift — bridge lanes & rateband reshuffle
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@loopship.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike coming — need upgrade options for May/June

Diego,

Heads up: our traffic forecast for the upcoming campaign shows a 3x token increase starting the week of June 1 and we need a path to increase committed capacity for the Hosted API. Current contract is 1.2M tokens/mo and we expect to need ~4.5M/mo for the next 3 months.

Questions:
- Can we add a temporary uplift for June–Aug with prorated billing?
- What are the rateband changes and per-route rate limits if we move to the next tier?
- Any recommended ops/SE steps to avoid latency/regression during the ramp?

We'd prefer a short-term bridge (3 months) with the option to convert to a higher monthly commit thereafter. Samir (cc'd procurement) — can you share any PO/approval constraints?

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform
Loopship

---
Attachments: none
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@loopship.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike coming — need upgrade options for May/June

Samir — thanks for the heads up. We can absolutely support a temporary uplift + conversion path. High-level proposal (details attached):

1) Bridge commitment: increase to 4.5M tokens/mo for June–Aug as a time-limited uplift.
2) Billing/proration: prorated billing for June (start date 2027-06-01) with a one-time credit for June of 20% if you sign the amendment by 2027-05-25.
3) Ratebands & limits: moving to the next tier increases the token-based rateband (per-token unit price falls) and raises soft per-route rate limits from 600 RPS to 1,200 RPS. Hard throttles remain configurable; we recommend a soft-throttle guard during the first week.
4) Ops checklist: Ben has a short SE checklist for cache warm-up, KV pre-warm, and model pinning to avoid cold-starts.

I've attached the first-pass term amendment and our onboarding checklist. If that looks good, I can send a DocuSign and lock a June 1 start.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Diego@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood_term_amendment_v1.pdf (PDF), ops-onboarding-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Spike coming — need upgrade options for May/June

Quick technical notes from SE standpoint — tagging the ops items you asked about: Samir, you can share this with your infra team.

- Routing/Rate limits: we can route traffic across 3 model variants for resilience. Per-route soft limits should be raised to 1,000 RPS as an initial step, with an automated fallback to the quantized variant at 85% CPU utilization. Hard throttle stays at 1,500 RPS to protect shared pools.
- KV/prefix cache warmup: recommend a 48–72 hour warmup window. We'll provide a warmup script (attached as part of the sandbox load test report) and a monitoring dashboard tile to watch cache hit rate.
- Latency: expected p50 increase ~10–20ms on the larger commit due to wider batching; p95 should remain within SLA if we enable the soft-throttle policy.
- Sandbox: ran a targeted load test with your sample traffic — results attached. We recommend a staged rollout: Week 0 (small uplift, 20%), Week 1 (50%), Week 2 (100%).

Link to the sandbox folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-loopship-loadtest

I'll coordinate a 30-minute runbook review with your infra on Thursday if that works.

- Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
